q: Where do staff uniforms, safety shoes and PPE go in our carbon footprint?
title: Uniforms and PPE in Scope 3
short: They are purchased goods, so they belong in Scope 3 Category 1. Use quantities and materials from the invoice where you have them, such as pieces of cotton or polyester uniform and pairs of safety shoes, and a spend-based estimate for the rest. They are usually a small line.
audience: HR, admin and EHS teams at factories

ul: Uniforms, aprons and coats: count pieces and fabric type.
Safety shoes, helmets, gloves, goggles and ear protection.
Disposable PPE such as masks and nitrile gloves, which can add up in pharma and food plants.
Laundry of uniforms by an outside service is a purchased service, also Category 1.
Activity-based: pieces x a per-piece factor for the material, where a supplier or database gives one.
Spend-based: invoice value excluding GST x a factor for the product group, stating the factor's source and price year.
Disposal of used PPE is Category 5, waste.

p: For most manufacturers uniforms and PPE are a small share of Scope 3. Estimate once by spend; if it is under a few percent of your Scope 3, keep the spend method and say so.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase and service invoices; it uses quantities where the invoice shows them and otherwise gives a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based with wider uncertainty.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Category 1 purchased goods and services
